findings.subject: Branching signs, factors and units
findings.assessment: Ionization uses one parent removal and two daughters W and E-B-W over the slower-electron half-domain, one net new free electron, and one binding cost B. Excitation retains one daughter and records its effective cost separately. Number-conserving nonnegative interpolation also conserves energy. SI area, eV-to-joule, collision rate n*sigma*v, stopping b in eV/s, and G=T*G_physical scaling are consistent.

findings.subject: Causal source and disjoint ledgers
findings.assessment: The augmented linear system implements dx/du=Gx+u*a from zero initial state. Heat, H/He binding, H/He excitation and cutoff kinetic energy are disjoint absorbing energy ledgers. Ionization counts repair the free-electron number balance. Low-band crossing counters are excluded from the conservation ledger and do not double-count heat.

findings.subject: He total rate and printed BED sharing are an explicit hybrid
findings.assessment: He Q_total=0.8841 differs from Q_df=0.9130416667 implied by the printed continuum polynomial. Printed K_BED=1.1860 also differs from 2-Ni/N=1.19496. Normalizing the nonnegative slower-electron shape defines a legitimate conditional branching kernel but does not reconcile the atomic sources or certify physical accuracy.
findings.implication: atomic_G02 remains UNRESOLVED; cannot promote the model as a consistent NIST atomic replica

findings.subject: CCC excitation energy semantics
findings.assessment: The 27 adopted first-zero table energies are explicit effective excitation costs. He 2^1P uses 21.1156 eV while the independently read NIST level is 21.2180 eV. Native table coverage, units, positivity and hashes were checked; a spectroscopic target-state energy certificate was not obtained. A conserved effective-energy ledger does not resolve this difference.
findings.implication: Excitation reservoirs are atomic-energy bookkeeping, not a solved photon spectrum, prompt photon count, or absorption model

findings.subject: NIST CGI comparison
findings.assessment: The pre-numerical addendum records actual external HTTP500 failure and retains the original CGI comparison as NOT_EVALUATED. The executed published-equation integral check is only an algebraic/units oracle. Its numerical agreement is not substituted for an independent CGI result.

findings.subject: Independent time propagation and grid convergence
findings.assessment: DOP853 independently checks propagation on 240 active nodes with the same G, not an independent final 4800-node physical calculation. The reported 1.3928%/1.1529% refinement changes concern cumulative low-band crossing energy/count. Instantaneous crossing rates, pointwise spectra, and diagnostic heat partitions do not inherit a separately certified continuum error bound.

findings.subject: Coulomb closure, source projection and cutoff
findings.assessment: The min(classical, quantum) logarithm is an adopted leading-log matching prescription. Its preselected -1/2 sensitivity is not a physical uncertainty bound. Linear grid projection and the 0.1 eV ghost boundary introduce finite-grid effects, including near-boundary early absorption and low-band assignment of projected source just above 10 eV. Cutoff kinetic energy is retained separately from heat.

findings.subject: High-birth heat, low-energy heat and terminal comparison
findings.assessment: 42.5648% is total high-birth stopping-heat power relative to direct low-birth stopping heat. Only 2.3565% is the additional high-birth heat generated at E<=10 eV relative to that same direct low-birth reference. The terminal comparison uses the same frozen operator and current injection; it is not an IGM history or original FS10 reproduction.

findings.subject: One-thread project policy and historical runtime provenance
findings.assessment: The original R002 thread count was not recorded and is not retroactively inferred. A predeclared focused run fixes the five thread-control variables to 1, checks both loaded OpenBLAS pools at one thread, and reports /proc Threads=1. It reproduces all compared final observables exactly and the saved 21-time trajectory endpoint within the stated normalized tolerance. The initial resource-admission failure is preserved and the repaired resource estimate retains the mandatory reserve.
